input_prompt: `throttle.py` implements a token-bucket rate limiter: `make_bucket(capacity, refill_rate_per_s, now)`, a private `_refill(bucket, now)` that adds `elapsed * refill_rate_per_s` tokens (capped at `capacity`) and advances `bucket["last_refilled_at"]`, and `try_consume(bucket, now, cost=1.0)` which calls `_refill` then deducts `cost` if enough tokens are available. Implement a NEW function `try_consume_burst(bucket, now, costs)` that attempts to consume a LIST of costs against the SAME bucket in one call: call `_refill(bucket, now)` exactly ONCE at the start (not once per item, so refill timing never drifts mid-burst), then greedily attempt each cost in list order, deducting tokens only on success, and returning a list of per-item bools -- a failed item must NOT stop the loop, since a later, cheaper cost may still succeed. Include a regression test named exactly `test_try_consume_burst_allows_later_cheaper_cost_after_earlier_failure` with a bucket that has enough tokens for a cheap cost but not an earlier, more expensive one in the same `costs` list, asserting the cheaper later item still succeeds.
